newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian church leaders oppose canonising last tsar.
newsitem.headline: Russian church leaders oppose canonising last tsar.

text.p: A top council of the Russian Orthodox Church has decided not to recommend canonising Russia's last tsar Nicholas II, killed by Bolshevik revolutionaries in 1918 with his family, church officials said on Thursday.

"After a study of the state and religious activities of the last Russian tsar, the commission does not find a sufficient basis for his canonisation," Metropolitan Yuvenaliy told the High Clerical Council.
The council, which is made up of bishops and debates important church matters, took its decision on Wednesday.
It referred the matter to a wider church assembly for further consideration, but its decision reflected divisions and opposition in the church over making the tsar a saint.
The tsar was the head of the church as well as the government before the Bolshevik revolution,
Nicholas, his wife and their children were murdered in the Urals city of Yekaterinburg on July 17, 1918, just months after the revolution which paved the way to more than 70 years of communist rule.
